text.tspan: Everyday English - C1 - 2026/10/23 - 01 - Essay
Furniture, light and space shape an everyday room.
Pexels · 13977663
Making a room your own
The decision to arrange a room may appear ordinary, yet it exposes a recurring tension between arrangements that make life manageable
and experiences that resist being prescribed. A defensible approach combines proportionate preparation with a willingness to reconsider
whose interests a plan serves.
Preparation has value because giving everyday objects a clear place makes the room easier to use. In the present case, we keep keys in a
bowl beside the door. Such an intervention is modest, but that modesty is its strength: it removes a foreseeable obstacle without claiming to
determine the entire experience. Structure is useful to the extent that it releases attention rather than consuming it.
That argument requires a qualification, however: small personal choices make a space feel familiar. For instance, we place a favourite
photograph where we can see it from our chair. An arrangement that appears efficient from one standpoint may impose costs elsewhere.
Listening to those affected is therefore not an optional gesture of goodwill; it supplies information without which the plan cannot be adequately
evaluated.
The resulting principle is one of proportion. Preparation deserves support when it clarifies responsibilities and protects time, while
responsiveness prevents it from hardening into an end in itself. To judge the experience well is to examine both what the arrangement
enables and what it may inadvertently exclude.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete example. Conclude
by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write about an experience of your own.
Compare your first answer with this question: What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example. (Model: The two reasons are
that giving everyday objects a clear place makes the room easier to use and that small personal choices make a space feel familiar. One
example is that we keep keys in a bowl beside the door.)
